title: The Spatial Harness: Bringing Agents to the Canvas — Max Drake, tldraw
talk_summary: Max Drake demos tldraw's spatial harness: agents operate on an infinite canvas, with single-shot teaching, an agent starter kit, multi-agent 'fairies', and a dependency-graph task app where each node launches a coding agent. The transferable ideas are visual agent state, dependency-graph work management, orchestrator wait/review handoffs, and code-mode scripting against app APIs; most of the talk is canvas UX, not measured engineering.

takeaways.technique: Dependency-graph task board with launchable agent nodes
takeaways.what_they_do: They render tasks as a dependency graph and make each node a coding agent that can be kicked off, so blockers and next work are visible in one view.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's a dependency graph, but each of these tasks um is a a coding agent that you can kick off

takeaways.technique: Glanceable agent state instead of chat logs
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents expose visible working/waiting/orchestrator states so a human can monitor many agents without reading transcripts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I don't have to read a chat in order to know what's actually going on. I can look at the state of the agents.

takeaways.what_they_do: An orchestrator agent creates/assigns a task, waits for worker completion, then is notified and prompted to review the result.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's going to get notified. It's going to get prompted in order in order to review.

takeaways.what_they_do: They expose the app's editor instance through a local server so agents write plain JavaScript against it instead of being limited to a fixed tool UI.
takeaways.evidence_quote: has a server that lets any agent uh for example my cloud code uh write just plain JavaScript against the against the editor

takeaways.what_they_do: The agent changes its view to inspect relevant canvas objects, analogous to searching a codebase rather than loading everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It changed its view in order to see um what was you know the other stuff that was on the canvas.
